Messages.Author: Darkelf
Messages.Body:
Sequence of combat:

Vampire A declares an action.

Vampire B tries to block.

"No stealth played, action is blocked and combat begins"

Vampire A doesn´t maneuver.

Vampire B doesn´t either

"Round at close range"

Vampire A declares its strike: Superior version of Form of Mist (combat ends
continuing the action at +1 stealth)

Vampire B controller plays Claws of the dead (protean in both decks,
interesting) and a Rotschreck.

Is that possible?

We haven´t found enough acclaration in the Official C, Rulings and Errata.
There´s a sentence that says: "Cannot be played in response to an
announcement of a strike (or other effect) that is not effective at the
current range."

I think that the Rotschreck can not be played under that circunstances, but
other people think that you can.

Another cases in wich could exist some confusion would be, for example:

- Vampire playing CotD has 0 hand damage.

- Vampire A plays dodge instead of Combat ends.

Darkelf

You can: Rotschreck is playable if a blocking minion threats to deal
aggravated damage. In your example that#s definetely the case. Rotschreck
ends combat immediately, so the strike resolution phase is never reached,
thus: No combat ends due to Catatonic Fear.´

>

>
> - Vampire playing CotD has 0 hand damage.

Well, if there’s no threat of inflictiing aggarvated damage, Rotschreck
cannot be played. The threat would be there if that vampire played Lucky Blow
though.

>
> - Vampire A plays dodge instead of Combat ends.

He goes to torpor - as in the first case, strike resolution is never reached.
Rotschreck is an interesting card as you can see in those
Malk-out-of-tum-combat decks posted a while ago (check Legbiter's deck
archive at legbiter.tripod.com - by the way, all links were dead when I
checked a few days ago. Has that been fixed, Lasombra (or whoever runs the

Yes, if B declares his strike as "hands".

Messages.Author: John Whelan
Messages.Body:
I'm bored, so I'll answer this one.

On Mon, 11 Sep 2000, Darkelf wrote:

> Vampire A declares its strike: Superior version of Form of Mist (combat ends
> continuing the action at +1 stealth)
>
> Vampire B controller plays Claws of the dead (protean in both decks,
> interesting) and a Rotschreck.
>
> Is that possible?

I believe yes. Rotschreck can be used both offensively and defensively.
In case that "seems wrong" for intuitive reasons, here's a rationale for
you.

Rotschreck is a defensive instinctual vampiric response, that saves them
from destruction in certain situations by sending them prematurely to
torpor. However, most instinctive responses can operate at inconventient
times ... and not to your particular benefit. One might, for instance,
vomit at the sight of something unusually disgusting and unsanitary, even
though there may be no rational reason for believing that anything you
recently ate was tainted. Or like fainting (going into shock) at the
sight of someone ELSE's injury. Similarly, the proximity of a source of
aggravated damage might sent a vampire to torpor, even if he had no
*rational* reason for believing it would effect him.

So Vampire B sees Vampire A sprout those incredibly nasty-looking claws,
and his instincts kick in ... even though he knows that his "Form of
Mist" will take effect before those claws can quite reach him.

> We haven愒 found enough acclaration in the Official C, Rulings and Errata.
> There愀 a sentence that says: "Cannot be played in response to an

> announcement of a strike (or other effect) that is not effective at the
> current range."

That merely means (for instance) that you cannot play Rotschreck in
response to a long-range aggravated hand strike. (Justifiying playing
Rotschreck in such a case might be stretching the above rationale just a
little too far).

> I think that the Rotschreck can not be played under that circunstances, but
> other people think that you can.
>
> Another cases in wich could exist some confusion would be, for example:
>
> - Vampire playing CotD has 0 hand damage.

I believe 0 aggravated Hand damage counts as "no aggravated damage" for
Rotschreck purposes. If you attempt to strike for "no damage" then
there is nothing to be classified as aggravated.

> - Vampire A plays dodge instead of Combat ends.

Rothschreck still affects him.
